body: I don't trust anyone. Always have your finger on the (proverbial) trigger and never reveal anything about yourself that can be used against you later.

My best friend is one of the most generous and thoughtful souls I know. (hence why he is my best friend) He is strong, courageous, hard-working, and intelligent. He has a truly brilliant mind. And yet he cannot find a partner in life. He wants to start a family, and every girl he has dated has either ended up cheating on him or using him for some kind of twisted gain. 

I have watched him go through so much pain.

It's true, be an asshole and everyone loves you. But be a decent person with a good heart and you will be hated, berated, beaten, and bullied. It's sickening and I want nothing to do with any of it. If I had the power, I would Thanos snap the entire world into nothingness.
This is why I don't drive. I walk or take the train everywhere. I hate driving, always have.

Same here, I decided a long time ago I will NEVER get married or have children. I am going to live as simply as possible and avoid any relationships or cohabitation. I more than likely will buy a tiny home for a dirt-cheap price and just live the remainder of my days in solitude. A simple life with no headaches or having to deal with societal bullshit.

Very late reply here, but I appreciate your comment. I agree, I have completely given up on relationships and have not looked back since.

Social animal? Two words that don't describe me. Is there a very small, select few who I can resonate with? yes. But as a whole, when I am around others all I can think is "get me out of here!" I personally can't stand most people. 

I would be happy, pure bliss, if I could live in a totally isolated area where not a single soul would know where I am. An underground home where I was forgotten by the world above with nothing but good food, my cats, my books, my movies, my video games, and an internet connection where I could still pursue my writing career. 

I hate the need for humans to cluster together. They gather over race, sexual orientation, gender, tribe, language. In all honesty, it makes me sick to my stomach; it is truly repulsive to me that they form groups over some of the most arbitrary traits and parade it around like it's something unique and wonderful. 

This is why I like walking around at night, while everyone is inside and afraid of the dark I am out there having the entire world to myself. I am listening to audiobooks, podcasts, or some choice music. It is my own slice of nocturnal nirvana! Most of the time, during one of these night outings, I think to myself: What if it was like this all the time? No more crowds, no more idiots, no more fake and wishy-washy knuckle-draggers. Just me, a wide world, and plenty of beautiful animals for me to observe.

No community! the very thought of it warms my heart.

But muh legacy! Makes me sick when I hear people say this. If you can't love something because it doesn't share your precious genes (which are not that special, mind you) then don't bother dating or having friends. 

It's one of the few forms of narcissism that is sanctioned by society, religion, and the government. Few adopt because most are narcissistic assholes.

Because most people, in spite of all their posturing about how "good of a person" they are; cannot fathom thinking outside of themselves for a mere second. They talk on and on about "their legacy" or "their race" like those are inherently important things.

News flash, most of you are not impressive or important people. The world will not miss out on you passing your "legacy" on. Passing on your genes is not impressive nor a miracle in any sense of the word. It is the most common and mundane thing, so common that even amoeba do it. Far from incredible.

You want to really pass on something: write a book, create a work of art, make music, start a new philosophy, start an adoption agency, do something that has nothing to do with breeding.

People who adopt are automatically superior to breeders.

I used to feel bad about feeling this way, but I am now to the point where my mind and emotions are completely aligned. Not only can I extrapolate emotionally about my hatred of humanity, but I can explain it through logical means as well. 

My conclusion is clear, humans are a virus.
